name: TPS60500DGSR
title: TPS60500, TPS60501, TPS60502, TPS60503: 250-mA step-down charge pumps, adjustable, 3.3 V, 1.8 V and 1.5 V
summary: The TPS6050x parts are switched-capacitor step-down converters that turn 1.8 V to 6.5 V into a regulated output of up to 250 mA, using two flying capacitors plus input and output capacitors and no inductor. The TPS60500 is adjustable from 0.8 V to 3.3 V with an external divider; the TPS60501, TPS60502 and TPS60503 are fixed at 3.3 V, 1.8 V and 1.5 V. The chip picks among 1/3x, 0.5x, 2/3x and linear (LDO) conversion by the input-to-output ratio and the load, regulating by skipping pulses up to about 150 mA and linearly above. It has an open-drain power-good output, soft start, current limit, thermal shutdown and an active-low enable that cuts the load off from the input in shutdown. The TPS60500DGSR is the adjustable part in the 10-pin VSSOP on a 2500-piece reel.
key_figures: 40 µA typ, 75 µA max at IOUT = 0 mA

circuits.title: Typical application, 1.8-V output from a Li-ion cell
circuits.description: A fixed-output member of the family, set for 1.8 V, runs from a single lithium-ion cell. Two 1-µF flying capacitors sit across C1F and C2F, 2.2 µF bypasses the input and 10 µF holds the output. FB is tied straight to OUT, as on every fixed-voltage version. R pulls the open-drain PG line up to the output, and an external signal on EN switches the converter off (high) or on (low).

circuits.title: TPS60500 with adjustable output
circuits.description: The adjustable TPS60500 with its output set by a two-resistor divider: R1 from the output to FB, R2 from FB to ground, VO = 0.8 V × (R1 + R2) / R2. Cc, 10 pF, sits across R1. The flying capacitors are 1 µF each, the input capacitor 2.2 µF and the output capacitor 10 µF, for loads up to 150 mA. R is the pull-up for the open-drain power-good output.

circuits.title: TPS60503, 1.5-V output up to 150 mA
circuits.description: The fixed 1.5-V TPS60503 with the minimum parts: two 1-µF flying capacitors, 2.2 µF at the input and 10 µF at the output, enough for up to 150 mA. FB joins OUT directly because the divider is inside the chip. R pulls PG up to the output; EN low turns the converter on.

circuits.title: TPS60503, 1.5-V output up to 250 mA
circuits.description: The same 1.5-V converter set up for its full 250-mA rating. Above 150 mA the output needs at least 22 µF, met with two 10-µF capacitors in parallel (Cout1 and Cout2), and the input capacitor grows to 4.7 µF. The input range starts at 3.15 V for this load.

circuits.title: DSP supply with sequencing
circuits.description: Two rails for a DSP from one input of 3.5 V to 6.5 V, each good for 150 mA: the TPS60503 makes the 1.5-V core rail and a TPS77133 LDO makes the 3.3-V I/O rail. Pulling ENABLE low starts the charge pump. When its output is up, PG rises (pulled up by the 10-MΩ resistor) and turns on the NPN transistor, which pulls the LDO enable low against its 1-MΩ pull-up. The LDO then brings up 3.3 V, and its RESET output, pulled up by 47 kΩ to the I/O rail, releases the DSP reset. The 10-µF capacitor on each rail is the value recommended for stability; the DSP may need more capacitance.

circuits.title: LC post filter on the output
circuits.description: An extra inductor L(P) and capacitor C(P) after the 10-µF output capacitor cut the ripple further. The converter part is the 1.5-V TPS60503 with its usual capacitors; the filtered rail VP(out) carries up to 150 mA. Measured ripple for several capacitor and inductor choices is in the LC post-filter table: with a 0.1-µH inductor and 0.1-µF X7R capacitor at 100 mA, about 20 mV peak to peak.

circuits.title: Dynamic voltage scaling for a DSP core
circuits.description: A TPS60500 running from a 3.3-V system rail feeds a DSP core at 150 mA and can be switched between 1.1 V and 1.5 V by the DSP itself. R2 (180 kΩ) and R3 (470 kΩ) divide the output into FB and give 1.1 V. A BSS138 MOSFET, T1, driven from a 3.3-V DSP port on DVS in, adds R4 (360 kΩ) in parallel with R3, which raises the output to 1.5 V. C(ff), 150 pF from the output to FB, is the fast-forward capacitor for better line regulation. R1 pulls PG up to the input; PG continues through R5 (330 kΩ) to an output node with C6 (470 pF) to ground.

circuits.title: Internet audio player supply
circuits.description: One or two NiCd, NiMH or alkaline cells are boosted to a 3.3-V system rail of at least 100 mA by a TPS61010, and that rail feeds a TPS60503, which steps it down to a 1.5-V DSP core rail of up to 150 mA. Around the boost converter: L1 (10 µH) from the cell to SW, Ci (10 µF) at the cell, Co (22 µF) at VOUT, R3 and R4 dividing VOUT into FB, R1 and R2 dividing the cell voltage into LBI, R5 from VOUT to LBO, and Cc1 (10 pF) plus R(C) (100 kΩ) in series with Cc2 (10 nF) from COMP to ground. The charge pump has 2.2 µF at its input, 10 µF at its output and 1-µF flying capacitors, with R from the output to PG.

operation.text: The chip holds a clock oscillator, a reference, an error amplifier, two MOSFET-switched pump stages, start-up and shutdown circuitry, control logic and, on the fixed-voltage parts only, an internal feedback divider. The output is sensed and the switches are enabled only as needed to hold it, a skip-mode scheme used from no load to 150 mA; at heavier loads the part regulates linearly. Outputs from 0.8 V to 3.3 V are possible with inputs of 1.8 V to 6.5 V.
The ratio of input to output voltage and the load decide which of four modes runs: LDO, 2/3x, 0.5x or 1/3x. The internal circuitry changes mode by itself.

When no switched mode fits the ratio, switches 1, 2, 5 and 6 close and join the input straight to the output; the flying capacitors carry no energy. Up to the linear-skip current (150 mA typical) regulation works by turning MOSFETs 2 and 6 off; above it the on-resistance of the switch is controlled. Regulation needs at least 1 V between input and output.

Chosen when the input is more than 1.5 times the set output. In the first phase the two flying capacitors, paralleled, charge with the output capacitor in the current path; in the second they are stacked in series. Input current is then two thirds of the output current, so efficiency beats the LDO mode.

Chosen when the input is more than twice the output, for example 3.6 V to 1.5 V. Both flying capacitors and their switches work side by side, which lowers the path resistance against the other modes. They charge in series with the output capacitor, then discharge in parallel with it.

Used when the input exceeds three times the output (5 V to 1.5 V is one case). The two flying capacitors charge in series with the output capacitor, each to about VIN/3, then are placed in parallel with the output capacitor.

While VOUT is under 0.6 V, output current is limited to about 300 mA. Above 150 °C chip temperature the thermal protection starts cutting the available output current, reaching zero at 160 °C. The output current limit with VOUT above 0.6 V is 500 mA typical.

EN high switches every internal circuit off: input current falls to 0.05 µA and OUT draws at most 1 µA. The load is cut off from the input in shutdown, which preserves battery charge. Taking EN low restarts the part; with no load it is up in about 80 µs.
The converter starts when EN goes from high to low, and the pump stages begin switching at once. Until the output reaches 0.6 V the input current is limited to about 300 mA.

Every device has PG as an open-drain pin. It is held low in shutdown and whenever the output has lost regulation, and is released, to be pulled high by an external resistor, once the output passes 97% of nominal. The pull-up usually goes to VOUT or VIN; an unused PG pin is left open. Rising and falling delays are in the electrical table (td,r 100 µs to 200 µs, td,f 50 µs to 100 µs).

Four ceramic capacitors give the most output current and the best performance; other types work at lower currents or where more ripple is allowed. The output capacitor sets stability and must be at least 4.7 µF; above 150 mA, where the part is in linear mode, it must be 22 µF or more, which two 10-µF parts in parallel satisfy. Larger output capacitance lowers ripple. Flying capacitors below 1 µF are allowed but cut the power available, pushing the part into linear mode at lower load. The input capacitor lowers the source impedance, which helps efficiency and steadies the input current. Ceramic parts give the least ripple because their ESR is lowest. On the TPS60501 to TPS60503 FB must be wired to the output outside the chip.
The source has no special demands beyond being able to deliver the current that the chosen input voltage, output voltage and load require.

Every capacitor goes as close to the IC as it can, which is what keeps the output ripple low. The two-layer example puts the ceramic input and output capacitors right at the device, a ground plane on the top layer around the parts and a ground plane on the bottom layer, with the flying capacitors C1F and C2F beside the package.

Lowering a DSP core voltage while it runs at a lower clock saves power (runtime power control). In the example the TPS60500 runs from the 3.3-V system rail and switches its output between 1.5 V and 1.1 V by a MOSFET that changes the feedback divider. Targets: 1.5 V ±0.08 V and 1.1 V +0.1 V −0.05 V, 3 V to 3.3 V input, 150 mA output (10-Ω load). The divider resistors are kept large to keep their current small.

DSPs commonly need a core supply between 1 V and 2.5 V and an I/O supply of 3.3 V. In the example the core rail comes up first; PG from the charge pump then enables the I/O LDO, whose reset output releases the DSP. Input range 3.5 V to 6.5 V, 150 mA from each rail.
